messages.content:
You are an operations analyst for a small café. Goal: shorten the bad-case wait (90th-percentile wait, "p90") without breaking the owner's constraints.
You only learn about the café through tools. Call exactly one tool per turn.
Budget: 6 test_change experiments and 12 tool calls in total. Then you must call finish.
Code decides acceptance, not you. A plan is accepted only if: overall p90 improves by at least 10%; the paired 95% CI of the improvement excludes zero; it still improves with task times 30% shorter and 30% longer; and no order type's p90 gets more than 10% worse.
Work like a scientist: look at the bottleneck, form a hypothesis, test it, learn from the result, then test the next idea. Prefer cheap changes. Try combining changes that were accepted.
Use your experiments: test at least 3 different plans (single changes or combinations) before calling finish, unless the budget runs out.
Minutes in changes count from the start of the rush. Keep text short. finish.summary must contain no digits.

Rush: 90 min from 07:00; orders/hour per 15-min block: 45,45,45,45,45,45.
Order mix: drink 50%, food 20%, drinkFood 30%.
Staff: cashier 1; barista 1; kitchen 1; barista hands over orders.
Typical task minutes: order 0.8, drink 1.3, food 2.5, handoff 0.3.
Drink + food orders: made at the same time.
Hiring is allowed. Budget $250 for the first month. Costs: staff $20/hour for 22 rush days; batching $50; handoff point $150; express station $400; grab-and-go $200.
Allowed options (at most one per group; combine groups freely). Copy the changes exactly:
- More barista staff: +1 barista = [{"kind":"staff","station":"barista","delta":1}] | +1 barista 07:30–08:00 = [{"kind":"staff","station":"barista","delta":1,"fromMin":30,"toMin":60}]
- Grab-and-go: grab-and-go 30% = [{"kind":"grabGo","shareOfDrinks":0.3}] | grab-and-go 50% = [{"kind":"grabGo","shareOfDrinks":0.5}]
- Handoff point: dedicated handoff (1) = [{"kind":"dedicatedHandoff","staff":1}]
- Prep mode: sequential prep = [{"kind":"prepMode","mode":"sequential"}]
Today (simulated): {"p90":28.1,"median":17.8,"byType":{"drink":{"p90":24.3,"median":16},"food":{"p90":26.9,"median":18.3},"drinkFood":{"p90":29,"median":20.6}},"stations":{"cashier":{"busy":52.4,"maxQueue":4.7},"barista":{"busy":87.8,"maxQueue":17},"kitchen":{"busy":82.3,"maxQueue":7.1}}}
Busiest station: barista (87.8% busy).

Code decides acceptance, not you. A plan is accepted only if: overall p90 improves by at least 10%; the paired 95% CI of the improvement excludes zero; it still improves with task times 30% shorter and 30% longer; and no order type's p90 gets more than 10% worse.
Work like a scientist: look at the bottleneck, form a hypothesis, test it, learn from the result, then test the next idea. Prefer cheap changes. Try combining changes that were accepted.
Use your experiments: test at least 3 different plans (single changes or combinations) before calling finish, unless the budget runs out.
Minutes in changes count from the start of the rush. Keep text short. finish.summary must contain no digits.

Rush: 90 min from 07:00; orders/hour per 15-min block: 45,45,45,45,45,45.
Order mix: drink 50%, food 20%, drinkFood 30%.
Staff: cashier 1; barista 1; kitchen 1; barista hands over orders.
Typical task minutes: order 0.8, drink 1.3, food 2.5, handoff 0.3.
Drink + food orders: made at the same time.
Hiring is allowed. Budget $250 for the first month. Costs: staff $20/hour for 22 rush days; batching $50; handoff point $150; express station $400; grab-and-go $200.
Allowed options (at most one per group; combine groups freely). Copy the changes exactly:
